question: Stubborn agents (workers, zealots), W-MSR, Friedkin–Johnsen, polarisation

metric_definitions.manifesto: fixed per seed: ORACLE manifesto of the default world (ζ = 0.05, DeGroot)
metric_definitions.anchor_share: Δ_off(k) / Δ_on(k), Δ = E(k workers) − E(0 workers); off = attempt_cap 0

metric_definitions.within: mean over non-zealot voters of TV(v_i, own regional mean)
metric_definitions.bimodal: share of non-zealot voters with P < 0.1 or P > 0.9 (P for the fixed b)
metric_definitions.disagreement: long runs: mean TV(v_i, mean v) over free voters (not zealot, not worker)
metric_definitions.fj: fixed point of the cascade-off DeGroot dynamics (harmonic extension of the stubborn opinions)

test_families.anchor_positive: Δ_off(k) = E(k workers, cascade off) − E(0) vs 0, Wilcoxon, 3 rules × 3 k, Holm (9)
test_families.wmsr_minus_degroot_worker_value: worker value Δ(k) under W-MSR F − under DeGroot, 2 rules × 3 k × {cascade on, off}, Wilcoxon, Holm (12)
test_families.zealot_persuasion_change: persuasion (policy − none) at ζ minus at ζ = 0, 3 rules × 3 ζ × {pay_split, planner}, Wilcoxon, Holm (18)

deviations: Arm A 'fixed campaign' is played with two policies (pay_split and the ORACLE planner), each against 'none' in the same cell.
One fixed manifesto per seed in every cell (the DeGroot ζ = 0.05 ORACLE manifesto), not re-optimised per rule or ζ.
Long runs (T = 200) are experiment-side (the game allows T ≤ 10), cascade off, no campaign after the round-1 workers.

parity.cell: W-MSR F = 1, k = 10 workers in round 1, cascade on
parity.note: statistical tolerance max(0.01, 3·SE); converts scaled by N
